# v2.90

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.88-dev, v2.89-dev and
v2.90-dev**. Stable has been on v2.87 since early September, so everything below
is new to production installs.

Most of it is security hardening from a review of the areas that have grown since
the last one. One item is not: **automatic backups have not been running since
v2.70** — see **Check your backups** immediately below.

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

## Check your backups

**Automatic backups have not run on any installation since v2.70.** An enabled
schedule saved your settings but never took a backup, and the Backup page
reported "the cron entry could not be installed" while pointing at
`/etc/cron.allow` — advice that could not have helped, because the real cause was
that the application deliberately runs under a restricted account that is not
permitted to write the system's scheduling tables at all.

- Anything taken with **Run Backup Now**, and anything you downloaded manually,
  is unaffected.
- If your most recent automatic backup is older than you expect, that is why.
  **Take a backup now from Run Backup Now before updating.**
- One case may have masked this: a server upgraded *from* a version before 2.70
  may still have a leftover entry running backups on whatever schedule was set
  back then — so backups may have been happening, just not on the schedule the
  page displayed. The update clears that leftover and the schedule shown on the
  page becomes the one that runs.

After updating, open **Admin → Backup & Restore** and confirm the Automatic
Backups panel shows no warning. The next scheduled run will appear in
`/var/log/training-tracker/backups.log` and as a new file in the backup folder.

## What's new

- **Changing your password now signs you out everywhere else.** The browser you
  make the change in stays signed in; every other session on that account ends
  the next time it does anything. If you change your password because you think
  someone else has it, that now ends their session too, rather than leaving it
  valid until it happens to time out.

- **An admin password reset does the same for the account being reset.**
  **Admin → Users → Reset Password** now evicts every session that user has
  open. That is usually the point of the reset, and previously it did not
  happen.

  Both are documented in the in-app help (**My Account** and **User
  Management**) and the README.

## Fixed

- **Automatic backups now actually run**, by the same scheduled-jobs mechanism
  that already runs updates and report exports. See **Check your backups** above.

- **A missed backup runs late instead of being skipped.** If the machine is off
  or busy at the scheduled time, the backup is taken at the next opportunity the
  same day rather than waiting until tomorrow.

- **The page shown at the end of connecting a cloud storage provider** (Google
  Drive, Box, OneDrive) has been rebuilt. It no longer repeats text supplied by
  the provider — you get a clear fixed message and the provider's own wording
  goes to the server log, where it is more use for diagnosis — and it confirms
  you are signed in as an Admin before it will render at all.

- **Two gaps in how requests are checked for permission have been closed**, one
  on a catalogue route and one in the shared request filter. Neither is known to
  have exposed anything on a normal installation; both are fixed, and the
  affected route now carries the same check every comparable route already had.

- **The "keep last N" setting on a scheduled export can no longer delete more
  than it should.** A non-whole number entered there used to be treated as zero
  *after* the housekeeping had already started, which cleared the folder instead
  of trimming it. The value is now rounded down and applied consistently, and the
  tidy-up only ever considers files.

## Hardened

- **Scheduled exports saved to the server now write inside one folder.** A
  **Local Filesystem** export delivers into the server's exports folder —
  `exports` in the application directory unless the new `EXPORT_ROOT` setting
  says otherwise. Enter a name such as `monthly` in **Output Path** for a
  sub-folder, or leave it blank for the folder itself. Anywhere else is refused
  both when you save the schedule and when it runs, so a schedule created before
  this release cannot quietly keep using an old location.

- **The backup folder picker stays inside the backups folder.** **Browse** opens
  at `backups` in the application directory — or wherever the new `BACKUP_ROOT`
  setting points — and cannot be navigated above it. This matches the rule
  **Save** has always applied, so no folder you could actually have used has been
  taken away.

- **Connection tests say less about the network.** **Test Connection** and the
  credential health checks report a short fixed reason — the credentials were
  rejected, the host and port could not be reached, or the server name could not
  be resolved — instead of repeating the underlying network error. The full
  detail goes to the server log. The same applies to the error recorded against a
  schedule when a delivery fails.

- **A connection test to an unresponsive host gives up in seconds** rather than
  after roughly two minutes, so checking all your providers no longer ties up the
  server while one of them hangs.

- **The update process no longer treats its own configuration as executable.** It
  reads the values it needs from `.env` from a fixed list of expected keys rather
  than running the file, and version numbers, release names and tokens are passed
  around as data, never assembled into commands. If you keep anything unusual in
  `.env`, only the keys the updater needs are read; everything else is ignored
  rather than interpreted.

- **Tighter file ownership for the scheduled-job logs.**
  `/var/log/training-tracker` and the files in it are now owned by root, with the
  application account writing through the group — matching how the update status
  and log files already worked. The update helper also gets a private temporary
  directory. Applied automatically; no action needed.

- **A missing service account is now a hard error, not a silent fall-back.** The
  update scripts drop privileges before running `npm install` and the build. If
  the unprivileged account was missing they used to carry on regardless. They now
  stop and tell you to run `deploy/install.sh`.

- **Stricter session-token validation**, and the same minimum-length rule for
  `JWT_SECRET` is now applied everywhere rather than in most places.

## Changed

- **The Backup page tells you if nothing can run your schedule.** On a server
  without scheduled jobs installed, enabling automatic backups shows a notice
  naming the one command to fix it, instead of implying a backup is coming. It is
  shown whenever the page is open rather than only when you press Save.

## Upgrading

This release adds **one database column** and applies automatically — no manual
step. Sessions already open keep working; they are only affected once that
account's password is next changed. The backup scheduling entry is installed by
the update itself.

Two optional settings are new, and both are only worth setting if you write
outside the application directory:

- **`EXPORT_ROOT`** — if a scheduled export writes to a folder outside the
  application directory (a mounted share, for instance), set this in `.env` to
  the folder that contains it and restart the service. Until you do, that
  schedule reports an error instead of running, and the error names this setting.
  Exports using the default location need no action.
- **`BACKUP_ROOT`** — the same, for the backup folder.

On a systemd host, a folder outside `/opt/training-tracker` also needs a matching
`ReadWritePaths=` line added via a drop-in, followed by `systemctl daemon-reload`;
the service is sandboxed and will otherwise be refused permission to write there.

Both are documented in `.env.example`, the README and the in-app help
(**Scheduled Report Exports** and **Backup & Restore**).
